facts.raw_span: asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the left side of his forehead, frontal scalp, and vertex area
Localized linear hair loss and hair thinning on the left scalp area
2 long, curved-line, depressed, alopecic patches on the left side of the vertex and frontal scalp area extending to the left eyebrow
lesions measured (length × width) 7 × 2 cm and 6 × 1 cm, respectively
Dermoscopic examination of the alopecic area revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation
broken hairs were not seen
result of a hair pull test was negative
Histopathologic examination shows predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis
inflammatory infiltrates between adipocytes with hyaline fat necrosis in the subcutis
Direct immunofluorescence: Positive with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels
Antinuclear antibody: Negative
Antidouble-stranded DNA antibody: Negative

rationales.F01: The presence of an asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove is consistent with several scalp conditions.
rationales.F02: Localized linear hair loss and hair thinning are common features of lichen planopilaris and frontal fibrosing alopecia.
rationales.F08: The histopathologic findings of predominant lymphocytic infiltrates and lobular panniculitis are characteristic of discoid lupus erythematosus and lichen planopilaris.
rationales.F09: Inflammatory infiltrates between adipocytes with hyaline fat necrosis are seen in discoid lupus erythematosus and lichen planopilaris.
rationales.F10: The positive direct immunofluorescence results support the diagnosis of discoid lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F11: The negative antinuclear antibody result makes discoid lupus erythematosus less likely.
rationales.F12: The negative antidouble-stranded DNA antibody result also makes discoid lupus erythematosus less likely.

frontier_selector.why: The evidence of localized linear hair loss and hair thinning on the left scalp area, along with 2 long, curved-line, depressed, alopecic patches, specifically supports Frontal fibrosing alopecia.
